paradoxes.text: The neutrality that keeps Ashgabat out of blocs also leaves it without a guarantor. The Trans-Caspian route to Europe needs the Caspian consensus that Russia and Iran withhold, and the Iran swap needs Iran's goodwill, so the policy that protects the regime also makes its export routes hostage to the very neighbours it refuses to join.

sources.title: Turkmen gas is back on Turkey's agenda

grand_strategy.reading: Turkmenistan runs the strategy of a state that has bought its safety with one rule, neutrality, and spends it on gas: every great power gets a stake in the pipeline, none gets a base. Two decades of this have made China the decisive partner and left the other routes as options rather than income. The dynastic handover of 2022 has not changed the rule, so the card reads the leadership as a continuity of the same strategy.

stances.note: Largest buyer by far: more than three-quarters of Turkmen gas exports go to China through the Central Asia-China pipeline (OSW, 2023), and the 2026 production plan of about 76 bcm is again built around China (PGJ Online, April 2026). Diplomatic relations since 6 January 1992 (Wikipedia index; tier 4 pointer). Bond - none: pure interest; Ashgabat's neutrality keeps it from any Chinese bloc. Trend warming on the gas volume is our reading of the production plan; a 2025 fall of 7 per cent in Turkmen flows to China (Interfax, June 2025) is noted but does not reverse it.

stances.note: Transactional, with no alignment: Russia has an embassy in Ashgabat and Turkmenistan one in Moscow, but Turkmenistan is outside the CSTO and keeps its neutrality. Gas is the only thick tie: Gazprom stopped buying in January 2016 over price and resumed in April 2019 (IntelliNews, tier 3). We found no 2025-2026 report of Gazprom volumes from Turkmenistan, so the gas status today is unverified. Russia is the former colonial power, but Soviet history is not a standing tie in Ashgabat's own framing, hence bond none. Grade is structural (no treaty, no troops), not rhetorical.

stances.note: A gas-for-gas swap: Turkmen gas goes to Iran and an equal amount of Iranian gas reaches Turkey. The BOTAS-Turkmengas deal of 10 February 2025 started on 1 March 2025 (S&P Global, March 2025), with 1.3 bcm expected by end-2025. The Iran cut-off of 2017 over arrears (Wikipedia, tier 4 pointer) shows the limit of the tie. Caspian boundary tension and Iran's theocracy keep it from friendship (Wikipedia index). Bond none: a joint Körpeje-Kordkuy pipeline and the Dostluk dam are interest, not kinship. Trend stable: the swap is the same logistics as before.

stances.note: The gas customer next door: Turkmenistan supplies up to 2 bcm a year to Uzbekistan under the 2023 agreement. Frictions are real and old: the Amu Darya water sharing and the shared Kokdumalak condensate field (Jamestown, older analysis). We found no 2025-2026 report of a water or border agreement. Bond - affinity: Turkic, Central Asian and Muslim, sympathy without a shared state project. Trend warming on the gas track only.

stances.note: Mirrors the AFG card (same sources, same reading from the other side). Work on the TAPI pipeline in Herat resumed in September 2024, and Turkmen officials expect the 130-km Herat segment by end-2026. Ashgabat has not recognised the Taliban state but has let the Taliban appoint diplomats to the Afghan embassy in Ashgabat (Eurasianet, 2022, cited in Wikipedia, not opened). Bond none: a transit and gas relationship with no shared identity. Trend warming: the pipeline is physical progress and the Taliban are the host; the security of the border is the open risk.

stances.note: Serdar Berdimuhamedov attended the Central Asia plus US summit in Washington in early November 2025 (dates vary by source, 6-7 November), met the US President separately and adopted two statements of intent on economic cooperation and cultural heritage. Turkmen state media frame the trip as positive neutrality (official statement, tier 1 for the statement only). The open disagreement is on reform: Washington has pressed privatisation and market opening, which Turkmenistan has not adopted (Wikipedia index, tier 4 pointer). Bond none: pure interest. Trend warming on the summit track only.

stances_toward.note: Turkmenistan builds the TAPI pipeline in Afghanistan with the Taliban as the host and transit state: work resumed in September 2024 and the Taliban ministry reports 101 km of pipe laid in Herat province by 6 Jul 2026 (self-reported, not independently verified); Ashgabat says its 130-km Herat segment will finish by the end of 2026. A partner by geography - Ashgabat's neutrality works for everyone - and the only Central Asian state the Taliban need for gas rather than rail. Herat alone cannot replace the Pakistani and Indian markets.
